purpose: Transport-only evidence that a Scheduled Runtime producer can publish a bounded result into a distinct disabled Scheduled Task used as a passive mailbox.
observations: Generations 1, 2, and 3 all published successfully using the same physical producer task and the same physical mailbox task.
The producer did not mutate itself; its one-shot execution lifecycle remained separate from mailbox mutation.
The mailbox remained disabled and did not execute; its last_run_time stayed historical while updated_at/title/prompt changed.
This is materially more repeatable than self-update of the currently executing Scheduled Task.
limitations: Three successful ordinary generations establish repeatability for the distinct-mailbox path, but recovery behavior and production request binding remain to be proven.
These first transport-only generations did not bind a real ACP request digest/blob.
Automations update exposes no compare-and-swap precondition on mailbox content.
Generation tags allow stale-data detection but do not by themselves prevent an old still-running producer from overwriting a newer mailbox value.
required_reclamation_invariant: Never recycle or advance a mailbox generation while any producer invocation authorized for the current generation may still be running. A mailbox is reclaimable only after the producer is known terminal, the mailbox relay has been durably accepted or the generation explicitly abandoned, and the trusted actuator records ACK/reclaim.
next_test: Generation 4 deliberate missing publication followed by same-generation delivery retry with unchanged logical_attempt, mailbox_generation, admission_nonce, relay_id and relay_nonce.
